findings.description: The policy grants ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:* and cloudwatch:* on Resource "*", giving this principal full control over four services including all S3 data, the ability to create/modify compute and execute arbitrary Lambda code. This violates least privilege and turns a single credential compromise into broad account-wide impact (CWE-732/CWE-284).

The Terraform output surfaces the access key secret material, causing the credential to be persisted in state and printed in plan/apply logs where anyone with read access to the state backend or CI logs can retrieve it. Long-lived keys should never be emitted as outputs.

A static IAM user access key is created with no rotation mechanism, and it is attached to the principal holding the wildcard ec2:*/s3:*/lambda:*/cloudwatch:* policy. Static keys do not expire and, if leaked, remain valid indefinitely with full access to those services.
The output publishes the deploy user's name, disclosing a valid IAM principal identifier that aids an attacker in targeted credential/enumeration attacks. Low impact on its own.
